Sylvia — thank you for the opportunity to put this together, and our condolences on the circumstances behind it. Everything in it comes from the records and from one MLS® pull run this week: every semi-detached sale within a kilometre of 23 Newlin since August, and every one for sale now. We have not been inside, so the number here is an estimate from the records and the photographs of the neighbours' homes; the walkthrough turns it into a pricing strategy, and most of what follows is written to be confirmed there. One thing shapes the document: an estate that wants to sell soon has one real advantage over every other listing on the street — the house is empty and can be shown from the first day — and the plan is built around using it. Our reading of the evidence is stated once, at the end, and labelled as ours.

Section 01 · The property

A 1961 four-bedroom semi-detached two-storey on a ravine lot, held by one family since 1986 — offered by the estate, vacant and ready to show.

23 Newlin Crescent is a two-storey semi-detached home in Glenfield-Jane Heights, on the quiet crescent that backs onto the Downsview Dells ravine. Four bedrooms upstairs on 1,308 sq ft above grade, one full and two half baths, a mutual driveway with no garage, and a 28 × 116 lot that MPAC records as abutting the ravine. The home has been in the same hands for forty years and is being sold by the estate; we have not walked through yet, and this document assumes original condition throughout. The house is vacant while the estate clears it, which is the one advantage an estate sale has over every other listing on the street: it can be shown from day one.

Two things are true at once. The pocket is liquid — 58 freehold sales so far this year at 98% of list, one in six over asking, and the two-storey semis in particular have sold at 99.5% of list with half of them over asking. But the district's price level is lower than last year's: TRREB's W05 semi-detached average is down 6% and its median 4% on a small sample, while the city's semi-detached average, up 2%, is being carried by neighbourhoods a long way from Jane and Sheppard. Buyers for a four-bedroom semi here are present; they are paying the pocket's number, which this year has been $715,000 to $823,000 for seven of eight two-storey sales.

Board statistics stop at the district line, so we pull our own MLS® data on the 1st of each month — every sale in the five regions — before the board publishes. During your listing that means we see a shift in this pocket and respond to it while other agents are waiting for the report.

Section 04 · What the pocket did

Fifty-two semi-detached sales in the community this year. The two-storeys are the pocket's entry point; the bungalows and backsplits sell for more.

SYNERGY's own extract — every freehold sale in Glenfield-Jane Heights from January to September — puts the subject's form at the bottom of the pocket's price ladder. Semi-detached two-storeys ran $715,000 to $985,000 with an $800,500 median; the bungalows and raised bungalows, the pocket's main stock, ran $770,000 to $945,000 with an $860,000 median; the backsplits and sidesplits, bigger inside, took a $931,500 median. On Newlin Crescent itself, 77 Newlin (a bungalow on a 148-foot lot, no garage) sold for $820,000 in May and 73 Newlin (a four-bedroom backsplit, no garage) for $935,000 in July — and 37 Newlin, an original raised bungalow on the ravine, went conditional this week at $799,900.

Section 05 · What each sale tells us

Two-storey semis in this pocket run from $715,000 needing work to $823,000 updated — and the originals, of any form, are closing at $790,000 to $811,500 this month.

53 Giltspur Dr · Jane end of the pocket

$823,000

Sold August 10 · 99% of list · 25 days

The ceiling for the form. The only two-storey semi in the search area sold since August with a finished look: newer kitchen with quartz and stainless, newer floors, pot lights, paint and roof, a two-bedroom basement suite with its own entrance, a detached garage and a ravine lot — 1,509 sq ft, 200 more than 23 Newlin. It is also at the Jane end of the pocket, the weaker side, which is why its updates and suite did not carry it past $823,000. Strip the updates, the suite and the garage and you are at the number a well-kept original four-bedroom on the ravine should bring.

148 Giltspur Dr · Jane end of the pocket

$715,000

Sold August 1 · 102% of list · 3 days

The floor. Listed for "investors, renovators" at $699,999 on a 75 × 103 corner lot with a two-car garage, and bought in three days at $715,000. Three bedrooms, original throughout, a basement that needs finishing. It shows what a two-storey semi in this pocket is worth when the work is left to the buyer — and that pricing under the evidence here produced one bid at the floor, not a bidding war. The same street as 53 Giltspur, the same Jane-end location.

32 Buckland Rd · Sheppard & Arleta

$811,500

Sold October 13 · 99% of list · 22 days

The most recent sale in the pocket, two weeks old. A bungalow held by one family for sixty years — original, cared for, staged — with a finished lower level and separate entrance and a built-in garage. Listed at $789,000, raised to $819,000 after the first week's showings, sold at $811,500. It is not the subject's form; bungalows take a premium here. It is the clearest evidence of what buyers are paying this month for an original semi that presents well.

73 Kanarick Cres · Sheppard & Jane

$800,000

Sold September 4 · 100% of list · 3 days

Original, no garage, two entrances to a finished basement, 1,300 sq ft — the same size as 23 Newlin on a different plan. Listed at $798,800 and sold in three days at $800,000. The form is a bungalow, but on parking and condition it is the closest match in the set, and it says a $799,900 list price in this pocket finds a buyer in days when the house is clean and the number is right.

86 Arleta Ave · Sheppard & Arleta

$790,000

Sold October 1 · 99% of final list · 20 days

The pricing lesson, in one listing. A vacant 1981 raised bungalow with two kitchens on a 62-foot lot, listed September 11 at $899,900 — virtually staged, "to show you what can be done" — with no takers; reduced to $799,900 on September 22 and sold nine days later at $790,000. Same month, same pocket, same conclusion as the two conditional listings in Section 07: the market will pay about $800,000 for an original semi here, and will not pay for the asking price to be tested first.

The pattern

Two-storey semis in the search area have sold between $715,000 (needs work, Jane end) and $823,000 (updated, with a suite, Jane end) since August. Every original semi of any form that closed in September and October did so between $790,000 and $811,500, in 3 to 22 days, at 99–102% of its final list — and the one that asked for more sat until it stopped. 23 Newlin is a four-bedroom two-storey on the ravine, on the Sentinel side of the pocket, in condition we have not yet seen: the evidence puts it in the $775,000–$815,000 band, and the walkthrough decides where.

The two Giltspur sales bracket the form: $715,000 when the work is left to the buyer, $823,000 when it has been done and a suite and garage come with it. 23 Newlin sits between them — original but, we assume, maintained; four bedrooms where both had three upstairs; a ravine lot like 53's; no garage like neither; and on the Sentinel side of the pocket rather than a block off Jane, which is worth something and which both Giltspur sales lacked. The September and October closings and the two conditional listings then fix the month: original semis here are trading at $790,000 to $811,500, and two two-storeys found their buyers at $799,000 and $799,900. The midpoint of $795,000 is the reconciliation, and at $608 per square foot it sits between the two-storeys' $545–559 and the bungalows' $615–692 — where a four-bedroom original with a ravine lot and no garage should.

This estimate is built from the records and the photographs on file; we have not been inside. A walkthrough — the kitchen and baths, the floors, the roof and mechanicals, what the basement is, and what the ravine looks like from the back of the house — is what turns it into a pricing strategy. Until then, treat it as a well-supported starting point rather than a number to list at.

Section 07 · Who you would be competing with

Four two-storey semis are for sale within the search area. The two priced at $799,000–$799,900 found buyers inside a month; the two above $900,000 have not.

Five semi-detached homes of the subject's form are listed within 1 km, and the pattern in the sold evidence repeats in the actives. 14 Thurrock — the closest thing to a twin of 23 Newlin on the market — listed at $799,000 on September 30 and went conditional in 28 days. 37 Newlin, four doors down and on the same ravine, went conditional at $799,900 after four months of asking for more. 11 Dixiana tried the opposite: a four-bedroom two-storey listed at $699,900 for an offer night that produced nothing, repriced to $799,900, and still waiting. Above $900,000, 52 Bengal and 30 Clubhouse are larger homes with garages that have reduced and relisted without a buyer.

Section 08 · Two ways to price it

Two ways to price it — and why the number is not final until we have walked through.

Both columns assume a launch within a week of the walkthrough and the clear-out, with photography, drone and the ad campaign ready on day one. The range in Section 06 is an educated estimate from the records; the strategy is finalized once we have seen the house.

The pocket's own history decides the approach. Every original semi that closed since September was priced at or within 1% of the number it sold for and went in 3 to 22 days. The two that asked for more — 86 Arleta at $899,900, 37 Newlin at $999,000 — sold only after they stopped. And the one that priced under the evidence to start a contest, 11 Dixiana at $699,900, got no offer at all and is still waiting at $799,900.

Two ways to price it

Choose your level of service

Three packages, the same duty of care in every one — and for an estate sale, the one that takes the clearing, cleaning and preparation off your hands.

Every package includes the full professional obligations we owe you: presenting all offers, acting in your interest, and complete disclosure. What differs is how much of the preparation and marketing we take on.

For 23 Newlin we recommend Signature, and for this file we add what an estate needs: we order the bin, arrange the crews to clear what is left, and have the house professionally cleaned before photography — at no extra charge. The comparable sales make the case for presentation: in this pocket the two-storeys that showed well sold at or over asking, and the ones that did not sat.

What we do for your property

A ravine lot, four bedrooms and a house that can be shown tomorrow — the campaign leads with all three.

Most of the pocket's listings are three-bedroom bungalows facing another house. 23 Newlin has the fourth bedroom, the ravine behind it and vacant possession — the three things a family buyer in this bracket cannot find on the same street. The campaign leads with the lot from above, then the rooms, and the showing calendar opens the day it goes live.

Production

  • Estate clear-out first — bin, crews and a professional clean, coordinated by us before a camera comes in
  • Professional photography — the house empty, bright and clean — shot and edited for MLS®, print and social
  • Aerial drone — the ravine lot and the Dells behind it; the one picture a buyer cannot get from the sidewalk
  • Floor plans — both levels measured and drafted — four bedrooms on one floor is the headline

Exposure

  • MLS® and full syndication — REALTOR.ca and every major portal, day one
  • Paid digital advertising, 24/7 — across our six pages for the life of the listing, aimed at family buyers in the west end and the agents who serve them
  • Collaborator posts — the tour reel on all six team pages at once, then to the large pages we work with
  • Agent network — a personal call to every agent who has sold a semi in Glenfield-Jane Heights this year — fifty-two of them
  • Database — featured to 30,000 contacts, including first-time buyers moving up from condos

On the ground

  • Painting and touch-ups — where the walkthrough says they will return more than they cost
  • Staging — light staging of the main floor and primary bedroom, so an empty original house reads as a home
  • In-house legal review — the estate's authority to sell, the offer conditions and the closing — checked before anything is signed

Questions sellers ask

The things most people want to ask, answered before you have to.

Why not list higher and come down if we have to?

Because this pocket reads the days. 86 Arleta asked $899,900, got nothing for eleven days, and sold at $790,000 nine days after it came down to $799,900. 37 Newlin asked $999,000 in June and found its buyer at $799,900 in October. Every original semi that closed since September was priced within 1% of what it sold for and went in 3 to 22 days. The price the evidence supports on day one is the shortest route to the best number — and for an estate with carrying costs, the shortest route is the point.

The house is full of forty years of belongings. Do we have to clear it before we list?

Yes — and you do not have to do it yourselves. On this file we order the bin, arrange the crews, and have the house professionally cleaned before the photographer comes, at no extra charge. What you want to keep comes out first; we handle the rest. A clear, clean, empty house photographs and shows the way the comparable sales that went in days did.

Should we renovate before selling?

No. 53 Giltspur had a new kitchen, new floors and a two-bedroom suite and sold for $823,000; the originals are closing at $790,000 to $811,500 without any of that. A renovation would not return its cost in this bracket, and it would cost the estate the months it wants back. Paint and touch-ups where the walkthrough says they return more than they cost — that is the line.

Does the ravine lot add value?

Yes, and the campaign leads with it. Most of the pocket's semis face another house across a driveway; 23 Newlin backs onto the Downsview Dells. It is one of the three things a buyer cannot find elsewhere on the street — the lot, the fourth bedroom, and a house they can see tomorrow — and the drone footage exists to show it.

Who signs, and what does the buyer's lawyer need from the estate?

The estate trustee signs, and the buyer's lawyer will want to see the authority to do so — the certificate of appointment, or the will and the documents that stand in for it until the certificate issues. Our in-house legal review goes through what is on hand before the listing agreement, so the first offer does not stall on paperwork.

Is there tax on the sale?

This is for the estate's accountant, and it is usually simple: the home is treated as sold at its value on the date of death, so the estate's gain or loss is measured from that date, not from 1986. Terrence is a CPA and will make sure the right questions are asked before the listing goes live — the date-of-death value is the one figure worth confirming now.

How long will it take?

The sales that were priced to the pocket took 3 to 25 days to an offer, and a 30–60 day close after that. 14 Thurrock, the closest thing to a twin of this house, took 28 days to a conditional buyer. Priced at the evidence, vacant and clean, two to three weeks to an offer is the reasonable expectation.

Who will I actually be dealing with?

Terrence, on every call, showing and offer. The team is behind the file — a Broker for the contract, a law-trained partner for the estate paperwork and the agreement, and licensed agents to cover showings — but one person is accountable to you, and it is the one whose name is on this document.
